title: A Semantic Framework for Reproducible Variational Quantum Algorithm Execution Records
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms are hybrid quantum-classical workflows whose results depend on many interacting choices, including the ansatz, Hamiltonian, optimizer, backend, shot count, noise model, mitigation method, random seed, stopping criteria, and software versions. In current practice, this information is often scattered across code, configuration files, logs, backend metadata, and paper descriptions, making executions difficult to reproduce, compare, debug, and reuse. This paper proposes an ontology-supported framework for representing Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) execution records as structured and machine-readable software engineering artifacts. The framework defines a Web Ontology Language (OWL) ontology for modeling the main entities involved in VQA experimentation, including algorithms, circuits, ansatzes, Hamiltonians, optimizers, backends, noise models, mitigation techniques, execution steps, software environments, measurement outcomes, and results. It further combines the ontology with Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) constraints for validating completeness and consistency, and SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language (SPARQL) competency queries for retrieving reproducibility-relevant information. We demonstrate the approach using Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) execution records, including a valid record and intentionally incomplete or inconsistent examples. The results show that the framework can represent complete VQA execution contexts, detect missing or malformed metadata, and support query-based inspection of information needed for reproducible quantum software experimentation.
summary: This paper introduces an ontology-supported framework to solve the critical problem of non-reproducible Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) execution records. By modeling all interacting components—from ansatzes and Hamiltonians to optimizers and noise models—using OWL, it creates a structured, machine-readable record. This allows researchers to rigorously validate completeness and query the exact context needed for reliable quantum software experimentation.
main_problem: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) generate results dependent on numerous interacting choices, making current execution records difficult to reproduce, compare, debug, and reuse.
main_result: The authors propose an ontology-supported framework that successfully models complete VQA execution contexts and can automatically detect missing or malformed metadata.
method: They use Web Ontology Language (OWL) to model key entities into a structured, machine-readable artifact, validating completeness with SHACL constraints, and enabling querying via SPARQL.
model_or_system: The framework models the entire hybrid quantum-classical execution loop of VQAs, including components like ansatzes, Hamiltonians, optimizers, backends, noise models, and measurement outcomes. The motivating example is the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE).
key_observables: Final energy estimates, full execution context metadata (ansatz structure, Hamiltonian representation, optimizer configuration, shot count, random seed), and provenance records.
important_parameters: Ansatz parameters, noise model parameters, optimization convergence criteria, and software/backend versions are critical inputs.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption addressed is the fragmentation of execution context across disparate sources (code, logs, papers), which necessitates a standardized semantic representation for reliable reproduction.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general VQA workflow loop. Figure 2 provides an overview of the ontology structure connecting algorithm configuration to recorded outputs. Table 1 summarizes ontology classes by conceptual module.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of non-reproducible VQA records, proposes the OWL/SHACL/SPARQL framework, details its components and validation mechanisms using examples (like VQE), and demonstrates its utility in capturing full execution context.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial meta-layer for quantum computation research, addressing reproducibility—a major bottleneck when comparing results across different hardware platforms or algorithmic variations. It formalizes the necessary metadata structure for future benchmarking.
